info.name: Atlas — Workflow Engine API
info.description:
# Atlas — Workflow Engine API

Drive a running **Atlas** BPMN workflow engine from Postman: sign in, deploy models,
run instances, work user tasks, correlate messages, manage Modeler artifacts and
talk to the MCP transport. Every request documents what it needs and what it
answers, carries saved example responses, and asserts the status and shape of the
response in its *Tests* tab.

## Setup

1. Start a server (from the repository root):
   `ATLAS_ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-one' go run ./cmd/atlas serve --addr :8080 --data-dir ./atlas-data`
   — login is required by default; on a fresh data directory this seeds the user
   `admin` with that password.
2. **Import** this collection and the `Atlas (local)` environment, and select the
   environment (top right).
3. Set `baseUrl`, `username` and — as its **current value** only — `password`.
4. Run **Authentication → Log in**, then the **🚀 Golden Path** top to bottom, or the
   whole collection in the **Collection Runner**.

For machines (Newman, CI) use an API token instead of a password: put it in
`apiToken` and the collection sends `Authorization: Bearer …` on every request.

## Coverage

This collection is a curated, runnable tour of the most used endpoints — not the
whole API. The complete, always-current reference is the OpenAPI document at
`{{baseUrl}}/api/v1/openapi.json` (explorer: `{{baseUrl}}/api/docs`); see
**Health & Info → OpenAPI document**.

## Conventions

- Deploy and draft bodies are raw BPMN XML (`application/xml`); everything else is JSON.
- Variables use `{"variables": {name: value}}`.
- Keys are engine-assigned `uint64` numbers; instance and task keys are large,
  because they encode the partition in their high bits.
- Capped listings (`/tasks`, `/instances`, `/incidents`, `/audit`, `/approvals`)
  answer a page `{items, total, totalExact, truncated, nextCursor}`, never a bare
  array.
- Errors answer `{"error": "…"}` with a 4xx/5xx status.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
Every Atlas server requires a login unless it was started with `--auth=false`
(ADR-0195). Two credentials work, and every request in this collection accepts
either:

| Credential | For | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Session cookie** `atlas_session` | People | **Log in** once; Postman's cookie jar sends the cookie on every later request to the same host. Valid for 12 hours. |
| **API token** (Bearer) | Machines — Newman, CI, workers | Put the token in the `apiToken` environment variable. The collection's pre-request script then sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. |

**First start of a fresh server.** With an empty user store Atlas seeds one
administrator: username `ATLAS_ADMIN_USERNAME` (default `admin`), password
`ATLAS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — or, if that is unset, a generated password that is
written to the startup log **once** (event `auth.admin_seeded`).

**Reachable without a credential:** `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `GET /api/v1/info`,
`GET /api/v1/auth/providers`, the login-screen settings (`/api/v1/settings/theme`,
`/logo`, `/registration`), `/healthz` and `/readyz`. Everything else answers
`401 {"error":"authentication required"}` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`
header pointing at the OAuth protected-resource metadata (ADR-0200).

The folder runs in all three modes without editing anything: with a password
(*Log in* signs in), with `apiToken` set (*Log in* and the admin-only token
requests skip themselves), and against an open server started with `--auth=false`
(*Log in* skips itself).

**Log out** sits in the last folder of this collection, so that a run of the
whole collection keeps its session until the end.

item.name: Check whether a login is required

request.description:
Asks the server whether it enforces login, before you have signed in. The same
endpoint as *Who am I* below, sent first on purpose:

- **401** `{"error":"authentication required"}` — the server requires a login
  (the default). Run *Log in* next, or set `apiToken`.
- **200** `{"authEnabled": false, "user": null}` — the server runs open
  (`--auth=false`, for demos only); nothing in this folder is needed.
- **200** with `"authEnabled": true` and a `user` — you are already signed in.

Stores the answer as `authEnabled`; *Log in* and *Log out* skip themselves on an
open server.

exec: console.log(enforced ? 'This server requires a login.' : 'This server runs open (--auth=false): no login needed.');

request.description:
Exchanges a username and password for the `atlas_session` cookie.

- **Access:** public (this is the call that creates a session).
- **Body:** `{"username": "…", "password": "…"}`. The collection reads both from
  the environment: `username`, and `password` (type *secret* — enter it as the
  **current value** only, so it is never synced or exported). If you prefer the
  Postman Vault, replace `{{password}}` in the body with `{{vault:password}}`.
  Newman has no Vault: it treats `vault:password` as an ordinary variable name, so
  a command-line run then needs `--env-var 'vault:password=…'`.
- **200:** the user record (`id`, `username`, `roles`, `source`, …) and
  `Set-Cookie: atlas_session=…; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`, valid for 12 hours.
- **401** `{"error":"invalid credentials"}` — wrong username or password.
- **Throttling:** each account absorbs five failed attempts, then further attempts
  are refused until the budget refills (15 minutes for a fully spent account);
  each client address has its own, larger budget.

Skipped when `apiToken` is set (the token already authenticates every request) and
on a server that runs open.

exec: console.log('Log in skipped: ' + (pm.variables.get('apiToken') ? 'apiToken authenticates every request.' : 'this server runs open.'));
console.warn('401: check the username and password environment variables (the password is a secret: set its CURRENT value).');

request.description:
Says whether this server enforces login and who the current credential belongs to.
The quickest way to check that your session cookie or API token is being sent.

- **Access:** any signed-in principal. Without a credential it answers **401**
  like every other gated route.
- **200:** `{"authEnabled": true, "user": {"id", "username", "roles", …}}` with a
  session. With an API token `user` is `null` — a token is not a user account —
  and on an open server the answer is `{"authEnabled": false, "user": null}`.

Creates a machine credential (ADR-0194). This is what Newman, a CI job, a worker on
another host or a stdio MCP adapter should use instead of a person's password.

- **Access:** admin.
- **Body:** `name` and `scope` are required. Scopes: `full`, `worker`, `metrics`,
  `status`, `directory`, `inventory`, `landscape`, `events`. `expiresInDays`
  bounds the lifetime (`0` = never expires). `reach` limits a `landscape` token
  (required) or an `events` token (optional) to named projects/catalogues.
- **200:** the token record **plus the secret in `token`. The secret is returned
  exactly once** and never stored server-side; copy it now.
- **Roles:** a token carries its minter's *non-admin* roles. A `full` token minted
  by an admin can therefore do everything in this collection except the
  admin-only requests (API tokens, *Set instance variables*).

**Using it in Postman:** set the environment variable `apiToken` (current value)
to the secret. The collection-level pre-request script then adds
`Authorization: Bearer {{apiToken}}` to every request.

This request deliberately does **not** store the secret anywhere; it only keeps the
token's `id` so that *Revoke API token* can clean it up again. The three token
requests skip themselves when `apiToken` is set, because a token is never admin.

item.name: 🚀 Golden Path (run top-to-bottom)
item.description:
The five-minute tour: deploy a model, start it, work its first user task, and read
back what the engine now holds. Send each request in order, or run this folder in
the **Collection Runner**. Sign in first (**Authentication → Log in**).

Each step's *Tests* tab stores the ids it produced (`defKey`, `instanceKey`,
`taskKey`) in collection variables, so the next step needs no copy-paste, and
asserts the status and the shape of the answer — a green run means the server
behaved.

1. Deploy the `order-approval` model ([`order-approval.bpmn`](order-approval.bpmn))
2. List processes — the new definition is there
3. Start an instance — it parks on *Review order*
4. List the instance's open user tasks
5. Complete *Review order* with form data
6. List the definition's instances — still active, now on *Approve order*
7. Read the instance's variables — start and task data, merged
8. Read engine stats

The **User Tasks** folder then finishes this instance's second task.

request.description:
Deploys raw BPMN 2.0 XML — here the bundled `order-approval` model, identical to
[`postman/order-approval.bpmn`](order-approval.bpmn).

- **Access:** modeler.
- **Body:** the whole model, `Content-Type: application/xml`. A collaboration
  deploys one definition per pool.
- **200:** `{"key", "processId", "version", "deployments": [{"key", "processId",
  "name", "version"}]}`. `key` is the definition key every later request
  addresses. Deploying the same process id again — changed or not — creates the
  next `version` under a new key. A `warnings` array names references that will
  not resolve at runtime (for example a worker type nobody serves).
- **400:** the model does not compile; the error says where.

Stores `defKey` and `processId`.

request.description:
Starts one instance of the definition and runs the engine until it is idle:
`order-approval` parks on its first user task, *Review order*.

- **Access:** operator.
- **Body:** `{"variables": {...}}` — scalars, objects and arrays are all accepted
  and bind into FEEL as values, contexts and lists. Numbers keep their exact
  decimal text. `{}` starts with no variables.
- **200:** `{"definitionKey", "instanceKey", "stats": {...}}`.
- **404:** no deployment with that key.

To start the *newest* version by BPMN process id instead of a pinned key, use
`POST /api/v1/instances` with `{"processId": "...", "variables": {...}}`.

item.name: Applications, Drafts, Forms & DMN (Modeler)
item.description:
The design-time artifacts the browser Modeler manages: **applications** (the unit of
bundling, versioning and deployment, ADR-0128), **drafts** (saved, not yet
deployed diagrams), **forms** (form-js schemas for user tasks) and **DMN
references**.

`/api/v1/applications` replaced `/api/v1/projects`, which remains only as a
deprecated alias. The artifacts still name their application in a field called
`projectId` — the rename stopped at the API boundary, the stored tag did not.

The folder creates a throwaway application, fills it, validates and deploys it, and
removes everything again. Its ids (`postman-draft-sample`, `postman-review-form`)
are chosen so that it cannot overwrite somebody's work. Every request needs the
**modeler** role, except listing applications and reading forms.

item.name: MCP (AI agents)
item.description:
The same server speaks the **Model Context Protocol** over Streamable HTTP at
`/mcp`, so an AI agent can drive it with the `atlas_*` tools (ADR-0016). These are
JSON-RPC 2.0 calls.

`/mcp` sits behind the same login as the API (ADR-0196): the session cookie or an
API token works here too. A hosted agent connects with OAuth instead (ADR-0200).
The `Accept` header must allow both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`, or
the transport answers 406.
